title: test(plugin-detail): serve the explain double in the shape the hooks read (objectui#7996)
body:
Fixes #7996

## What was wrong

The `POST /api/v1/security/explain` double installed in `record-details.hideEmptyRetired-7129.test.tsx` answered `{ allowed: true }`, plus a matching `text` body. Neither hook that reaches this endpoint reads an `allowed` key:

- `useRecordEditable` reads `decision?.record?.visible` and returns early when it is not a boolean — fail open;
- `useRecordCrudVerdicts` reads `records` off the decision through a cast and `continue`s when it is not an array — fail open.

So the double resolved `ok: true` and the hook then took exactly the path it takes on `ECONNREFUSED`. The response body was inert, and the file was green for the reason it was green before the double existed.

The cost is forward-looking rather than current: this is one of the few landed examples of answering this endpoint, so a reader who copies it inherits a body the product ignores, and a future test meaning to pin a *specific* verdict writes `allowed` and quietly measures the fail-open branch instead of the verdict branch.

## The acceptance test — run FIRST, before anything changed

Triage's probe is falsifying, and it is the whole card in one line: replace the served body with an empty object and see whether the file still passes.

Run against the unmodified file at `6a0d1a435`. The mutation was proven on disk before the run (anchor count 1 to 0, replacement count 0 to 1, blob hash `5fe1f01c9b96e4` to `a3ca724049f4dc`) and restored by `git checkout HEAD -- path`, with the restore proven by an empty `git diff HEAD` and a blob hash identical to the HEAD blob:

```
served body during the probe:
    json: async () => ({}),
    text: async () => '{}',

PROBE_EXIT=0
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

An empty body passes. The reading could not distinguish a served verdict from a connection failure. **The card's premise holds — it is not falsified.**

## What the double answers now

Converged on the in-repo example objectui#7307 batch 1 landed, in the two shapes the hooks actually read: `{ record: { visible } }` for a single `recordId`, and `{ records: [{ recordId, visible }] }` for a batched `recordIds`. One payload feeds both `json()` and `text()`, so the two cannot drift into disagreeing about what the route answered.

## The verdict did not move, and that is the point

The file passes 3/3 before and after, identically. `useRecordEditable` initialises `allowed` to `true` and its fail-open path leaves it there, and the batched lookup's only consumer rules on `recordVerdict !== false` — so `true` and the absent verdict are the same value at every read site. A diff that changed which assertions hold would have done something other than this card. Nobody should read the green suite as evidence that the change was inert *by luck*: it is inert by the identity just named, and the probe above is what measures that the old body was inert for a different and unwanted reason.

## Which requests this file actually makes

Measured with a recording double writing to a file sink — temporary, not committed, restored the same way. Four calls, all to the explain route, all single-`recordId`:

```
2  url=/api/v1/security/explain  body={"object":"crm_opportunity","operation":"delete","recordId":"O1"}
2  url=/api/v1/security/explain  body={"object":"crm_opportunity","operation":"update","recordId":"O1"}
```

So the `record` branch is the live one here, and the batched `records` branch is not exercised by this file. It is carried for the reader who copies this double into a grid suite, which is exactly the copy hazard the card names; the comment says so in those words rather than leaving a silently unreached branch.

An instrument warning worth passing on, and the same shape as the one in the dispatch order: my first attempt at this measurement used `console.log` inside the double and recorded **zero** calls, which reads exactly like "the double is never invoked". It was the instrument, not the tree — those lines never reached the captured output. The file sink is what produced the reading above. Suspect the instrument before the tree.

## Scope boundaries, deliberately

- One double. Siblings reported, none swept.
- Neither hook touched. They fail open by design and that design is not on trial here.
- No assertion added or changed. Note that batch 1's landed doubles also carry a recording router plus an `afterEach` that fails on any non-explain URL — that is an assertion, so it is deliberately **not** adopted here even though the rest of the example is.
- Changeset with empty frontmatter, declaring no release: the file sits under a released package's `src/`, so the presence gate requires a declaration, and nothing published moves.

## Verification

| run | result |
| --- | --- |
| baseline, before any change | exit 0 — Test Files 1 passed, Tests 3 passed |
| empty-body probe (the acceptance test) | exit 0 — Test Files 1 passed, Tests 3 passed; premise confirmed |
| after the change | exit 0 — Test Files 1 passed, Tests 3 passed, identical |
| `@object-ui/plugin-detail` full suite at `ab0fa67de` | exit 0 — Test Files 183 passed, Tests 1756 passed |
| `@object-ui/plugin-detail` type-check | exit 0 — both `tsc --noEmit` and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` |
| eslint on the changed file | exit 0 |
| `check-changeset-presence.mjs` | exit 0 — empty frontmatter accepted as the explicit exemption |
| `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` | exit 0 |
| `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` | NOT GOVERNED — 2 paths checked against 5 governed surfaces, none matched |

Heavy runs went through the shared serialisation lock in the sibling checkout; the closure build and the package suite each reported `VERDICT command-exit 0`.

The type-check is not optional on this file: its party 3 is a compile-time assertion that only `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` can see, and the double now carries typed parameters. An earlier type-check attempt failed with `Cannot find module` across the workspace packages — that was an unbuilt dependency closure, a prerequisite gap rather than a red gate, and the run above is after building the closure.

Repo-wide lint and the rest of the farm are CI's run, not this seat's.

## Clause-2: no

A test double's response body. Counted off this diff: added `export` lines 0, removed `export` lines 0, production files under `src` changed 0, out of 61 added lines across 2 files.

That count on its own does not prove the answer, and should not be read as if it did: a zero for *added* exports says nothing about a changed or removed one, and nothing about a declarable key added to an already-exported shape. The substantive reading is that the only two files in the diff are a test file and a changeset with empty frontmatter — no exported symbol, no declarable key, nothing published moves.

Session, written as a code span so it survives a later body edit: `https://claude.ai/code/session_012EpHzwH4wTy5sd7ibkD2yq`
